facts.fact: Vipeoples reports that Senegal's ECOWAS biometric identity card is produced under a contract with a Malaysian firm, with bill 21/2026 amending the founding law before the National Assembly on 29 September 2026.

Senegal's DAF director Ibrahima Dieng said national identity-card production resumed after the February 2026 cyberattack and that the databases used to produce national identity cards are available, intact and unchanged.

facts.fact: APS reports the DAF announced that national identity card production resumed on 1 April 2026 and enrolment restarted progressively in several centres, after a halt from a 5 February cyber-attack.
Senegal's national biometric ID system, implemented by IRIS Corporation from late 2016, had issued biometric IDs to more than 7 million citizens by IRIS's account.

facts.fact: Senegal's ECOWAS biometric ID card is in circulation, with card production resumed from 1 April 2026 after a cyberattack on the DAF and about 700,000 cards due for renewal, per the interior minister.
Bill 21-2026 amending the law that instituted the ECOWAS biometric identity card, to extend validity of cards in circulation, was sent back to committee by the National Assembly.

facts.fact: IPRES requires Senegalese pensioners to hold their ECOWAS national identity card to complete its proof-of-life campaign from 1 July 2026.
Access to the e-Senegal platform, launched 24 March 2026 by SENUM SA, rests on authentication with the Numero d'Identification Nationale (NIN) carried on the biometric identity card, per Ndarinfo.
